title: Top-down Traffic Scenario Generation via Joint Initial-Goal Diffusion and Trajectory Infilling

control_signal.value: Map and number of agents; optional hard constraints on initial state, goal state, both, or neither during trajectory infilling; optional guidance costs (distance to neighbouring agents and lane centre) on the high-level scenario.

control_mechanism.value: Infilling model trained with a randomly sampled constraint mode that sets predicted bridge-distance to zero at constrained endpoints; separately, a guidance-cost gradient perturbs the diffusion noise prediction during sampling.

base_model.value: Two-stage: DDPM over initial-goal pairs with QCNet-derived map encoder and differential-transformer traffic generator; a deterministic goal-conditioned infilling network that predicts offsets from a straight-line bridge.

datasets.value: Argoverse 2 Motion Forecasting dataset; five agent categories (vehicle, bus, pedestrian, bicycle, motorcycle).

metrics.value: Collision rate, off-road rate, distance to nearest lane centre; Jensen-Shannon divergence for speed, lateral deviation, local density, nearest distance; ADE, FDE and miss rate for infilling.

controllability_evidence.value: Infilling Table II: hard constraints on initial and goal states give ADE 0.52 m, FDE 0 m, MR 0%, versus PD-init (initial-state constraint) ADE 1.86 m, FDE 7.16 m, MR 43.84%. Initialisation: off-road rate reduced by 2.8%, speed JSD by 55.3%.

stated_limitations.value: Stochasticity only in high-level scenario; trajectory infilling is deterministic, limiting trajectory diversity per scenario. Table I also shows higher collision rate (9.80 vs 4.40 and 4.22) attributed to polygon-based map encoding.

notes: Mainly about interpretable initialisation plus infilling, not user-steerable generation; control is modest (endpoint constraints, realism guidance). Table I results were reported without guidance sampling.
